- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for the next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–7 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates in high-sentiment periods; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment >0.6 for last 5 days.  
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and price is trending, model often misses momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–7 days.
